import numpy as np

def get_robot_placement(human):
    # Retrieve relevant joint positions
    left_shoulder = human.get_joint_pos("left shoulder")
    right_shoulder = human.get_joint_pos("right shoulder")
    left_hip = human.get_joint_pos("left hip")
    right_hip = human.get_joint_pos("right hip")
    
    mid_shoulders = (left_shoulder + right_shoulder) / 2.0
    mid_hips = (left_hip + right_hip) / 2.0
    
    # Spine direction vector pointing towards head
    spine_vec = mid_shoulders - mid_hips
    spine_dist = np.linalg.norm(spine_vec)
    spine_dir = spine_vec / spine_dist if spine_dist > 1e-6 else np.array([1.0, 0.0, 0.0])
    
    # Torso midpoint shifted ~0.18m towards shoulders/head per orchestrator notes
    torso_center = (mid_shoulders + mid_hips) / 2.0
    target_point = torso_center + 0.18 * spine_dir
    
    # Lateral direction pointing towards the human's left side
    lateral_vec = left_shoulder - right_shoulder
    lateral_vec[2] = 0.0
    lat_dist = np.linalg.norm(lateral_vec)
    lateral_dir = lateral_vec / lat_dist if lat_dist > 1e-6 else np.array([0.0, 1.0, 0.0])
    
    # Place robot on the human's left side at a standoff distance
    standoff_dist = 0.75
    robot_pos = np.array([
        target_point[0] + standoff_dist * lateral_dir[0],
        target_point[1] + standoff_dist * lateral_dir[1],
        0.0
    ])
    
    # Orient the robot's x-axis directly towards the workspace target point
    dx = target_point[0] - robot_pos[0]
    dy = target_point[1] - robot_pos[1]
    yaw = np.arctan2(dy, dx)
    
    robot_rot = np.array([
        [np.cos(yaw), -np.sin(yaw), 0.0],
        [np.sin(yaw),  np.cos(yaw), 0.0],
        [0.0,          0.0,         1.0]
    ])
    
    return robot_pos, robot_rot

from data_collection.vision_utils import find_surface_projection
from robot_motion_generation.tool_orientation import orientation_from_spec
import numpy as np

def generate_trajectory(seed, robot, human, pc_human, normal_human, camera_pos):
    np.random.seed(seed)
    
    # Landmarks for spine estimation
    l_sh = human.get_joint_pos('left shoulder')
    r_sh = human.get_joint_pos('right shoulder')
    l_hip = human.get_joint_pos('left hip')
    r_hip = human.get_joint_pos('right hip')
    
    mid_sh = (l_sh + r_sh) / 2.0
    mid_hip = (l_hip + r_hip) / 2.0
    
    # 3 points along the spine from top to bottom (spine2 -> spine1 -> spine)
    pt_spine2_approx = 0.8 * mid_sh + 0.2 * mid_hip
    pt_spine1_approx = 0.5 * mid_sh + 0.5 * mid_hip
    pt_spine_approx = 0.2 * mid_sh + 0.8 * mid_hip
    
    # Surface projections
    p_spine2 = find_surface_projection(camera_pos, pt_spine2_approx, pc_human)
    p_spine1 = find_surface_projection(camera_pos, pt_spine1_approx, pc_human)
    p_spine = find_surface_projection(camera_pos, pt_spine_approx, pc_human)
    
    # Tool orientation specification
    TOOL_ORIENTATION_SPEC = {"tilt_deg": 40.0, "tilt_toward": [-0.0, -1.0, 0.0], "x_ref": [0.866, -0.5, 0.0]}
    
    # Helper to get surface normal and orientation
    def get_normal_and_orientation(pt):
        idx = np.argmin(np.linalg.norm(pc_human - pt, axis=1))
        normal = normal_human[idx]
        ori = orientation_from_spec(normal, TOOL_ORIENTATION_SPEC)
        return normal, ori
    
    n_spine2, ori_spine2 = get_normal_and_orientation(p_spine2)
    n_spine1, ori_spine1 = get_normal_and_orientation(p_spine1)
    n_spine, ori_spine = get_normal_and_orientation(p_spine)
    
    standoff_dist = 0.15
    
    # Waypoints
    # 1. Separated non-contact pose behind spine2
    wp_standoff_start = {
        "position": p_spine2 + standoff_dist * n_spine2,
        "orientation": ori_spine2,
        "velocity": 0.05,
        "force": 0.0,
        "planner": "RRT"
    }
    
    # 2. Touch point 1 (spine2)
    wp_contact_spine2 = {
        "position": p_spine2,
        "orientation": ori_spine2,
        "velocity": 0.03,
        "force": 0.0,
        "planner": "Point-to-Point"
    }
    
    # 3. Touch point 2 (spine1)
    wp_contact_spine1 = {
        "position": p_spine1,
        "orientation": ori_spine1,
        "velocity": 0.02,
        "force": 2.0,
        "planner": "Point-to-Point"
    }
    
    # 4. Touch point 3 (spine)
    wp_contact_spine = {
        "position": p_spine,
        "orientation": ori_spine,
        "velocity": 0.02,
        "force": 2.0,
        "planner": "Point-to-Point"
    }
    
    # 5. Lift clear of body from lower spine
    wp_standoff_end = {
        "position": p_spine + standoff_dist * n_spine,
        "orientation": ori_spine,
        "velocity": 0.03,
        "force": 0.0,
        "planner": "Point-to-Point"
    }
    
    # 6. Final retreat pose
    wp_retreat = {
        "position": p_spine + (standoff_dist + 0.1) * n_spine,
        "orientation": ori_spine,
        "velocity": 0.05,
        "force": 0.0,
        "planner": "RRT"
    }
    
    waypoints = [
        wp_standoff_start,
        wp_contact_spine2,
        wp_contact_spine1,
        wp_contact_spine,
        wp_standoff_end,
        wp_retreat
    ]
    
    target_point = p_spine2
    
    return waypoints, target_point

record.name: trajectory_assertions_passed
record.doc: Programmatic waypoint checks: at least one contact waypoint, force in {0, 2} N, planner in the allowed set, velocity < 0.05 m/s while in contact.

record.name: waypoints_reachable_frac
record.doc: Fraction of planned waypoints passing the IK reachability check from the current robot placement. Any unreachable waypoint means the trajectory cannot execute as planned; this can indict the robot placement rather than the waypoints themselves, so consider backtracking placement when the trajectory looks sensible.

record.name: contact_waypoints_on_target_frac
record.doc: Fraction of contact waypoints whose nearest body vertex lies on a task-target segment. Off-target waypoints usually mean a bad surface projection (e.g. a shoulder point landing in the armpit).

record.name: projection_normal_angle_max_deg
record.doc: Max angle between the surface normal at each contact waypoint's landed vertex and the direction from that vertex to the projection camera. Waypoints are surface projections along camera rays, so only a landing on a grazing or hidden surface — a fold, the body's side wall, a crevice like the armpit — shows a large angle (> 75 deg, flagged). On a curved body, 45-65 deg at the lateral edges is EXPECTED for full-coverage tasks and is not a defect; do not shrink coverage over it.

record.name: contact_segment_origin_dist_max_m
record.doc: Largest distance-to-body of the ORIGIN waypoint of any contact segment. force>0 at waypoint k means the segment k-1 -> k is executed in contact, so its origin must already be on the body. A large value means a free-space descent (typically from the ~0.1 m approach standoff) was mislabeled as contact, which drags the approach across the skin. Near 0 is correct and expected.

record.name: goal_obs_dist_mean_m
record.doc: Mean distance from the commanded goal-gripper keypoints to the nearest observed point-cloud point over contact-phase steps. Large values mean the high-level policy's weighted-displacement target is unsupported by observation. Some occlusion is unavoidable — never expect ~0 everywhere.

record.name: goal_obs_dist_max_m
record.doc: Worst-case contact-phase distance from the commanded goal-gripper keypoints to the nearest observed point. Flag scale is the gripper size (~10 cm). Never expect 0; investigate via the render when flagged.

record.name: link_clearance_person_mm
record.doc: Worst signed clearance, over every command step of the executed episode, of any robot link that is NOT meant to make contact (the tool and the fingers carrying it are excluded), measured exact mesh-to-mesh against the person. Negative = a structural part of the robot passes through the person. Every other robot_motion metric scores the PLANNED waypoints; this one scores what the arm actually did.

record.name: link_clearance_furniture_mm
record.doc: Worst signed clearance, over every command step of the executed episode, of any robot link that is NOT meant to make contact (the tool and the fingers carrying it are excluded), measured exact mesh-to-mesh against the furniture. Negative = a structural part of the robot passes through the furniture. Every other robot_motion metric scores the PLANNED waypoints; this one scores what the arm actually did.

record.name: link_clearance_room_mm
record.doc: Worst signed clearance, over every command step of the executed episode, of any robot link that is NOT meant to make contact (the tool and the fingers carrying it are excluded), measured exact mesh-to-mesh against the room. Negative = a structural part of the robot passes through the room. Every other robot_motion metric scores the PLANNED waypoints; this one scores what the arm actually did.

record.name: link_clearance_obstacles_mm
record.doc: Worst signed clearance, over every command step of the executed episode, of any robot link that is NOT meant to make contact (the tool and the fingers carrying it are excluded), measured exact mesh-to-mesh against the obstacles. Negative = a structural part of the robot passes through the obstacles. Every other robot_motion metric scores the PLANNED waypoints; this one scores what the arm actually did.

record.name: tool_clearance_min_mm
record.doc: Closest approach of the tool itself (sponge pad / scratcher tip) to the person over the episode, exact mesh-to-mesh. Unlike the structure metrics this is EXPECTED to go slightly negative -- a contact task presses the tool onto the skin -- so it is reported for context rather than judged as a penetration.

        "planner": "Point-to-Point"
    }
    
    # 3. Touch point 2 (spine1)
    wp_contact_spine1 = {
        "position": p_spine1,
        "orientation": ori_spine1,
        "velocity": 0.02,
        "force": 2.0,
        "planner": "Point-to-Point"
    }
    
    # 4. Touch point 3 (spine)
    wp_contact_spine = {
        "position": p_spine,
        "orientation": ori_spine,
        "velocity": 0.02,
        "force": 2.0,
        "planner": "Point-to-Point"
    }
    
    # 5. Lift clear of body from lower spine
    wp_standoff_end = {
        "position": p_spine + standoff_dist * n_spine,
        "orientation": ori_spine,
        "velocity": 0.03,
        "force": 0.0,
        "planner": "Point-to-Point"
    }
    
    # 6. Final retreat pose
    wp_retreat = {
        "position": p_spine + 0.15 * n_spine,
        "orientation": ori_spine,
        "velocity": 0.05,
        "force": 0.0,
        "planner": "RRT"
    }
    
    waypoints = [
        wp_standoff_start,
        wp_contact_spine2,
        wp_contact_spine1,
        wp_contact_spine,
        wp_standoff_end,
        wp_retreat
    ]
    
    target_point = p_spine2
    
    return waypoints, target_point

record.name: trajectory_assertions_passed
record.doc: Programmatic waypoint checks: at least one contact waypoint, force in {0, 2} N, planner in the allowed set, velocity < 0.05 m/s while in contact.

record.name: waypoints_reachable_frac
record.doc: Fraction of planned waypoints passing the IK reachability check from the current robot placement. Any unreachable waypoint means the trajectory cannot execute as planned; this can indict the robot placement rather than the waypoints themselves, so consider backtracking placement when the trajectory looks sensible.

record.name: contact_waypoints_on_target_frac
record.doc: Fraction of contact waypoints whose nearest body vertex lies on a task-target segment. Off-target waypoints usually mean a bad surface projection (e.g. a shoulder point landing in the armpit).

record.name: projection_normal_angle_max_deg
record.doc: Max angle between the surface normal at each contact waypoint's landed vertex and the direction from that vertex to the projection camera. Waypoints are surface projections along camera rays, so only a landing on a grazing or hidden surface — a fold, the body's side wall, a crevice like the armpit — shows a large angle (> 75 deg, flagged). On a curved body, 45-65 deg at the lateral edges is EXPECTED for full-coverage tasks and is not a defect; do not shrink coverage over it.

record.name: contact_segment_origin_dist_max_m
record.doc: Largest distance-to-body of the ORIGIN waypoint of any contact segment. force>0 at waypoint k means the segment k-1 -> k is executed in contact, so its origin must already be on the body. A large value means a free-space descent (typically from the ~0.1 m approach standoff) was mislabeled as contact, which drags the approach across the skin. Near 0 is correct and expected.

record.name: goal_obs_dist_mean_m
record.doc: Mean distance from the commanded goal-gripper keypoints to the nearest observed point-cloud point over contact-phase steps. Large values mean the high-level policy's weighted-displacement target is unsupported by observation. Some occlusion is unavoidable — never expect ~0 everywhere.

record.name: goal_obs_dist_max_m
record.doc: Worst-case contact-phase distance from the commanded goal-gripper keypoints to the nearest observed point. Flag scale is the gripper size (~10 cm). Never expect 0; investigate via the render when flagged.

record.name: link_clearance_person_mm
record.doc: Worst signed clearance, over every command step of the executed episode, of any robot link that is NOT meant to make contact (the tool and the fingers carrying it are excluded), measured exact mesh-to-mesh against the person. Negative = a structural part of the robot passes through the person. Every other robot_motion metric scores the PLANNED waypoints; this one scores what the arm actually did.

record.name: link_clearance_furniture_mm
record.doc: Worst signed clearance, over every command step of the executed episode, of any robot link that is NOT meant to make contact (the tool and the fingers carrying it are excluded), measured exact mesh-to-mesh against the furniture. Negative = a structural part of the robot passes through the furniture. Every other robot_motion metric scores the PLANNED waypoints; this one scores what the arm actually did.

record.name: link_clearance_room_mm
record.doc: Worst signed clearance, over every command step of the executed episode, of any robot link that is NOT meant to make contact (the tool and the fingers carrying it are excluded), measured exact mesh-to-mesh against the room. Negative = a structural part of the robot passes through the room. Every other robot_motion metric scores the PLANNED waypoints; this one scores what the arm actually did.

record.name: link_clearance_obstacles_mm
record.doc: Worst signed clearance, over every command step of the executed episode, of any robot link that is NOT meant to make contact (the tool and the fingers carrying it are excluded), measured exact mesh-to-mesh against the obstacles. Negative = a structural part of the robot passes through the obstacles. Every other robot_motion metric scores the PLANNED waypoints; this one scores what the arm actually did.

record.name: tool_clearance_min_mm
record.doc: Closest approach of the tool itself (sponge pad / scratcher tip) to the person over the episode, exact mesh-to-mesh. Unlike the structure metrics this is EXPECTED to go slightly negative -- a contact task presses the tool onto the skin -- so it is reported for context rather than judged as a penetration.
